blocks.text: Rose Wylie / Napoleon and Wild Flowers / Nov 24, 2026 – Mar 6, 2027 / Opening Reception: Tuesday, Nov 24, 5pm – 7pm /
David Zwirner 5-6/F, H Queen’s 80 Queen’s Road Central Central, Hong Kong Tuesday – Saturday, 11am – 7pm +852 21195900

David Zwirner is pleased to announce Napoleon and Wild Flowers , an exhibition of work by British artist Rose Wylie at the gallery’s location in Hong Kong. This presentation includes new and recent canvases, historical and multipanel paintings, and works on paper that together embrace Wylie’s tendencies toward striking contrasts and adventuresome composition.

Wylie has become known for her uniquely recognizable, colorful, and exuberant compositions that appear aesthetically candid, not seeming to align with any discernible style or movement, but on closer inspection are revealed to be wittily observed and subtly sophisticated meditations on the nature of visual representation itself. The artist has long been interested in exploring perspectival and compositional strategies other than—and along with—traditional Renaissance perspective, frequently making numerous iterations of a given motif as a means of advancing her formal investigation. Working in both single- and multipanel formats, she regularly juxtaposes apparently disparate imagery, creating visual rhymes and resonances that coalesce into a unified composition.

The title for this exhibition is taken from a new body of work by Wylie—a series of paintings depicting wildflowers that appear as enlarged botanical drawings—and a 2026 diptych that revisits her impressions of the Ridley Scott–directed biopic Napoleon (2023). In Napoleon and Wild Flowers , the artist celebrates her affinity for distinct contrasts by pairing this image of the namesake nineteenth-century French emperor, who is often identified with ambition and domination, with subject matter that has seemingly opposite associations. In a group of six new paintings and accompanying works on paper, Wylie magnifies her source material to larger-than-life proportions to confer prominence and status to common wildflowers.

This exhibition marks the artist’s second solo show with the gallery in Hong Kong and follows her largest-ever survey presentation, Rose Wylie: The Picture Comes First , at the Royal Academy of Arts, London, in 2026. This exhibition is a continuation of Rose Wylie: Henri, Egypt…Bette, Bear , which also took place at David Zwirner Paris this year.
